solutions.check: 26 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: see 21dn.
Conservative holding tongue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: prim, stiff and old-fashioned in manner
second meaning: saying nothing, keeping quiet

explanation.walkthrough: The capital C suggests a Tory politician refusing to talk, but the two halves are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone formal and reserved, and also someone who refuses to speak or give anything away.

clue.text: Dogs, say, usually on these, fall foul of setters

parts.note: surface reading: where four-legged animals normally stand
setter's reading: setters are dogs, so a setter falling over still lands on its hands and knees, so to speak

explanation.surface: A dig at crossword setters, who supposedly trip over a phrase about dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters here are the gun-dog breed as well as crossword compilers; the second half is a joke rather than extra wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals such as dogs normally walk with hands and feet, that is all four limbs, touching the ground.

clue.text: End of Trump, with dodgy image — has to swallow Republican quip

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters are bent out of order
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: final letter of the surname
taken as written, then mixed with the P
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A jibe about the Republican president's carefully managed public image.
explanation.walkthrough: The P joins IMAGE before the shuffle, giving EPIGAM, and the R is then slipped in to make EPIGRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, witty saying, so it is a kind of clever remark or one-liner.

clue.text: Stuff peer — "love cocky inside"

indicators.note: inside tells us the paired words sit within the word before them

parts.note: to peer is to look nosily, to pry
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
pert means cheeky or cocky

explanation.surface: Sounds like a crude instruction: a lord being told to stuff a lover inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuff looks like a verb in an order, but it is the noun meaning belongings; love as the letter O is a tennis convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Property is a general word for belongings or things owned, just as stuff is in casual speech.

clue.text: Stiff old monarch grabs you, as Brenda would say

indicators.note: grabbing something means clutching it, so the monarch's letters hold the other piece

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the late Queen, whose royal way of saying you was one

explanation.surface: A dead old king seizing someone, described in the Queen's own idiom.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye always called Queen Elizabeth II Brenda; her famously formal speech said 'one' where others say 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a corpse, and a goner is someone dead or past saving.

clue.text: Which gets your "babe" off?

parts.note: surface reading: what gets a lover in the mood, babe being slang for a partner
setter's reading: a gentle song that sends an infant off to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around babe invite the slang reading; getting off means dropping off to sleep, not anything racier.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a soothing song sung to settle a baby into sleep.

clue.text: see 18dn.
Luvvie covets this to bits?

definitions.meaning: first reading split as two words: what an actor wants is a role in a show
second meaning: into pieces, as in falling to bits

explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a gushing theatrical actor; read the answer as two words and it is the role such a person craves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes apart breaks into separate pieces, the same idea as falling to bits.

clue.text: Approaching the bloody dictator? Decline!

parts.note: approaching a place is going to it
Pol Pot was the murderous Khmer Rouge leader of Cambodia

explanation.surface: A question about visiting a tyrant, followed by a curt refusal of the invitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Decline looks like turning down the visit, but it is a verb meaning deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating through neglect, so it matches falling off or worsening.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Groped all over, pull out as fast you can

indicators.note: one word spreads all over the other, wrapping right round it

parts.note: to grope is to feel about with the hands

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to a groper to pull out and run away as quickly as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: Pull looks like part of the phrase 'pull out', but out is the shuffle signal acting on pull alone.
explanation.definitionFit: At full pelt is an idiom meaning at top speed, running as hard as possible.

clue.text: Due to split with "free" UN, erm, Cameron not so keen on it now?

definitions.text: Cameron not so keen on it now

indicators.note: splitting breaks things apart, so the words are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Political chatter about Britain breaking away to be free of the United Nations, with a hesitant aside about Cameron.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron, British Prime Minister, called the 2016 vote on leaving the European Union and resigned after losing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron called the Brexit vote expecting to win, lost it and his job, so he would rather regret that ballot.

clue.text: (& 22ac.) Tutor smitten with 'Free World' shit, say

indicators.note: smitten literally means struck hard, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher besotted with Western propaganda that the setter thinks is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Smitten looks like infatuated, but it signals the letters being beaten up; 'say' marks shit as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Swear words such as that one are often exactly four letters long, hence the general term for obscenities.

clue.text: Follower of old Italian is looking mad, right in the proverbial

parts.note: someone furious goes red in the face

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another word

parts.note: the proverbial is a coy stand-in for the swear word, as in 'up to your neck in the proverbial'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A disciple of some old Italian is fuming and up to their neck in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The old Italian is Garibaldi, whose volunteer soldiers in the fight to unify Italy wore red shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi's followers were called the Redshirts after their uniform, so one of them is a redshirt.

clue.text: Audibly loud ejaculation being talked about

indicators.note: audibly means as heard rather than written, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: the noise of a loud sneeze, an ejaculation in the old sense of a sudden outburst

explanation.surface: Smutty on purpose: an apparent discussion of a noisy sexual climax.
explanation.walkthrough: Ejaculation here is the old word for a sudden exclamation, and the sneezing noise is spelt atishoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the one under discussion or in dispute.

clue.text: Norm, showing resistance, gets erect, losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to take a stand is to resist
a crude sense of erect

explanation.surface: A man called Norm resists, then becomes aroused, then loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Norm reads as a man's name, but it is the definition; HARD drops its H to leave ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is an accepted benchmark or usual level, which is what a standard is.

clue.text: 'Yes' sod off on 'Yes' epic tour

indicators.note: off can mean gone bad or wrong, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then shuffled

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, with just the start of the following word attached

parts.note: only the opening letter of the band's name is used

explanation.surface: Someone telling the prog-rock band Yes to clear off on a sprawling tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes is the British prog-rock band known for very long songs; the setter takes only the Y of the second mention, a loose step.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Homer's poem about Odysseus's wanderings, an odyssey is any long eventful journey.

clue.text: (& 8dn.) Where there's a fervent belief in the USA

definitions.text: Where there's a fervent belief in the USA

parts.words: Where there's a fervent belief in the USA
parts.note: surface reading: a general remark about American faith or patriotism

parts.words: Where there's a fervent belief in the USA
parts.note: setter's reading: a specific region of the southern states known for evangelical Christianity

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers the swathe of the American South where conservative Protestant churchgoing dominates social life.

clue.text: A bit old to spin and iron rags

indicators.note: spinning turns things round and round, so the letters end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then shuffled
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Household chores: old clothes to go in the spin cycle and then to be ironed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rags looks like old cloths for laundry, but it is slang for low-grade newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a scornful word for a cheap newspaper, and the downmarket popular papers are collectively called this.

clue.text: Put down Carpenters' selection

indicators.note: a selection is a portion picked out of something, here a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone records a track from the Carpenters, the 1970s soft-rock sibling duo.
explanation.walkthrough: Put down sounds like writing down or recording music, which is the sense meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to write them into a record or register, the same as putting them down.

clue.text: (& 1dn.) Climax and keep going? No medal if you do

parts.note: a crude slang sense of climax
to last is to keep going or endure

explanation.surface: A smutty sexual tip that turns into a sporting observation about medals.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark sits with the bedroom joke; the definition is the sporting bit at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing at the very bottom of a race means missing out on gold, silver and bronze alike.

clue.text: see 13dn.
Doped athlete pic mysteriously communicated

definitions.note: past participle phrase for an adjective: describes how something is passed on

indicators.note: a doped person is drugged and befuddled, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A photograph of a drug cheat in sport leaked out in some secret way.
explanation.walkthrough: Mysteriously looks like the anagram signal, but Doped is; mysteriously belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathic contact passes thoughts between minds without speech or any known channel, an uncanny way of conveying messages.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Graduate dared to be screwy as Corbyn

parts.note: BE is a Bachelor of Engineering degree

indicators.note: screwy means crazy or out of kilter, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then shuffled

explanation.surface: A student daring to be as unhinged as the Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Corbyn, then leader of Britain's Labour Party, is known for his grey beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Corbyn famously has facial hair, so someone like him in that respect has a beard on their chin.

clue.text: A time Cyril abused, which is quite plain

definitions.note: a describing clause standing for the noun: the quality of being plain

indicators.note: abused means treated badly or misused, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sordid tale of someone called Cyril being mistreated at some point.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarity is the state of being clear and easily understood, as something obvious and unambiguous is.
